0.text: Silver hits record highs and these old coins are worth multiples of what you paid.

1.text: With silver near record highs in 2026, holding pre-1965 USA silver coins, often called junk silver

2.text: Junk silver refers to coins minted in the USA before 1965.

3.text: These coins were made with 90 percent silver and 10 percent copper
and they circulated as everyday money.

4.text: After 1965, the USA government stopped minting silver coins for general circulation.

5.text: Today it is a broader term for pre-1965 USA silver coins
including those that were heavily worn or damaged.
The silver content is what matters, not the grade.

6.text: Silver hit a nominal all-time high of 121.
That makes junk silver coins worth multiples of their face value.
Citi projected prices could reach 150 dollars per ounce later in 2026.

7.text: The most common junk silver coins are dimes, quarters, half dollars
All of them carry that same 90 percent silver content.

8.text: A pre-1965 USA quarter has a face value of 25 cents.
At 2026 silver prices, its melt value is many times higher.
That gap is exactly why collectors and investors seek them out.

9.text: Coins dated 1965 and later were switched to a copper-nickel clad composition.
They look similar but contain no silver.
Checking the date is the fastest way to tell them apart.

10.text: Junk silver trades at a small premium over spot price and is widely available from coin dealers
Because the coins are recognizable, they are also easy to resell when you need liquidity.
